title: Quote orders properly, keep quality steady, track six numbers
course_title: Women Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development

say: Quote orders properly, keep quality steady, and track six numbers.
This is the video for module two of Women Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development.
Growing businesses sell by order: a party tray, a set of uniforms, crates of eggs for a hotel. If you quote from habit, a big order can make you busy and poorer at the same time.

say: Every order has six cost lines. First, direct inputs: ingredients, fabric, feed or detergent.

panel.heading: The six cost lines of an order
items: Direct inputs: everything in the product
Packaging: packs, bags, labels, crates
Shared running costs: gas, power, fuel
Delivery, including the return trip
Labour: helpers plus your own hours
Payment costs: gateway, POS and transfer fees

say: Here is a worked example. The client will pay through a payment link.
Ingredients cost 38,500 naira. Packaging is 50 packs at 250 naira each, so 12,500.
Gas, delivery and a helper for the day add 14,000. Her own 10 hours at 1,000 naira add 10,000.
Total cost, 75,000 naira. That is 1,500 naira per pack.
Margin is profit as a share of the price. Aisha wants 25 percent, and the link fee is 1.5 percent. So 75,000 divided by 0.735 gives about 102,041 naira.

panel.heading: Quote it, then protect your cash
items: Price = cost ÷ (1 minus margin minus fee rate)
Round sensibly and check the profit
Take a deposit that covers what you must buy
Put the terms in writing, even on WhatsApp

say: She rounds to 2,050 naira a pack, 102,500 in total. Had she quoted 1,800 a pack from habit, her profit would be about 13,650 naira, roughly half, for the same work.

say: And never release goods because of an SMS or a screenshot. Scammers send convincing fake credit alerts, especially on large orders. Check inside your own bank or wallet app.

panel.rule: Confirm payment in your own app, never by SMS or screenshot.

say: Without a written standard, quality depends on mood, and the same complaints come back.

panel.heading: Quality without and with a standard

say: Write your steps on one page, with a check anyone can do: a time, a weight, a count. Then track your complaint rate: complaints divided by orders, times 100.
Blessing tagged every laundry bag and counted items in and out. Her rate fell from 2.5 percent to 1 percent while volume rose.

panel.heading: Quality without and with a standard

say: For food, follow the WHO Five Keys to Safer Food: keep clean, separate raw and cooked, cook thoroughly, keep safe temperatures, and use safe water.

panel.heading: Safety basics as you grow

cards.d: Keep clean, separate raw and cooked, cook thoroughly, keep safe temperatures, use safe water.
Ventilate, check hoses with soapy water, never leave hot oil, do not overload sockets.
Always outside, away from doors, windows and vents. Exhaust fumes have no smell and can kill.

say: With gas, cook in a ventilated space, check hoses for leaks with soapy water, and keep a fire blanket or extinguisher nearby. Do not overload sockets, and keep irons away from water.

say: Write the same six numbers each month: revenue, gross margin, net profit, cash at month end, repeat customer rate, and your own hours.
Watch profit and cash side by side. Titi's egg profit rose to 105,000 naira in Month 3, but a hotel still owed her 180,000 for eggs on credit, so her cash fell.
Many profitable small businesses close because they run out of cash. End every review with one written action.

say: Remember. Count all six cost lines. Use the margin formula, take a deposit, and confirm every payment in your own app.
